turns.query: We are analyzing the static disintegration images of three self-made methylene blue sustained-release tablet formulations with different HPMC ratios. All images were captured under the same experimental conditions. The dissolution medium is initially pH 1.2, and after 1 hour it is switched to pH 6.8. The experiment was conducted at a controlled temperature of  38 °C to simulate a slightly elevated physiological condition. The system is a flow-through cell with a flow rate of 1 mL/min. The total observation period is 24 h. Images were captured continuously and later sampled into batches. Each message you receive contains multiple images representing a time window (e.g.,  0–6 h, 6–12 h, 12–18 h, 18–24 h). Treat the images within the same window as observations from that time range rather than a single exact time point. These three formulations are all methylene blue sustained-release tablets, and their main difference lies in the ratio between HPMC K4M and HPMC 100lv. The first formulation is the low-viscosity formulation. In this formulation, methylene blue is 0.1436, silicon dioxide is 0.0501, magnesium stearate is 0.1274, microcrystalline cellulose is 9.6862, lactose is 9.686, HPMC K4M is 1.0624, and HPMC 100lv is 4.2484. The second formulation is the standard formulation, which is also the medium-viscosity formulation. In this formulation, methylene blue is 0.142, silicon dioxide is 0.0503, magnesium stearate is 0.1278, microcrystalline cellulose is 9.6893, lactose is 9.683, HPMC K4M is 2.5037, and HPMC 100lv is 2.8171. The third formulation is the high-viscosity formulation. In this formulation, methylene blue is 0.1446, silicon dioxide is 0.0502, magnesium stearate is 0.1276, microcrystalline cellulose is 9.6846, lactose is 9.6845, HPMC K4M is 4.246, and HPMC 100lv is 1.0653. Our optimization goal is to adjust the ratio between HPMC K4M and HPMC 100lv so that the cumulative release amount of the standard-viscosity methylene blue sustained-release tablet over the first 4 hours is increased to 105% of its original level.Concentration-time information will be provided later after the image-analysis stage, so for now please focus on the image-based disintegration behavior under the current experimental and formulation background.
